There can be no permanent arrangements that entrench Gaza's division or leave millions of people living under Hamas control. Thirdly, the trajectory in the West Bank and East Jerusalem remains deeply alarming. We're appalled by the violence in the West Bank on the 24th of July, in which four Palestinians and two Israelis were killed. We condemn violence on all sides and call for de-escalation. We urge the Israeli government to exercise restraint, to uphold stability and international law, and to ensure accountability for crimes. We're also alarmed by the massive incursion at the Haram al-Sharif Temple Mount on the 23rd of July by thousands of Jewish worshippers. The status quo on Jerusalem's holy sites is clear and should be respected. We're further concerned by reports of an incursion by Israeli forces on an UNRWA training center located near Qalandia refugee camp yesterday morning. These incidents form part of a broader deterioration in the stability and security of the West Bank, fueled by settler violence and Israeli government policies. One hundred and four Israeli settlements have been approved in four years, and billions of dollars allocated to speed up construction. Together, these represent a deliberate attempt to erode the possibility of a two-state solution. Madam President, the path to peace requires the parties to demonstrate political will needed to realize the promise of the comprehensive peace plan. We must now renew momentum across all tracks and deliver tangible change on the ground. That is the only route to a future based on a two-state solution that delivers peace, security, and dignity for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I thank you.
I thank the representative of the United Kingdom for her statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of Bahrain.

Madam President, at the outset, we thank the Deputy Special Coordinator for the Peace Process Dr. Al-Akbarah for his briefing, which reflected the troubling situation in the Palestinian territory. We also welcome all participating states. Allow me to address three points. First, despite the inability to achieve the desired progress in achieving the first phase the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict through a complete ceasefire and guaranteeing a complete and effective humanitarian response. However, we remain hopeful. We must make every effort to alleviate the suffering of the Palestinian people in Gaza and the West Bank. We remain hopeful due to the significant work of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza and the holding of the third official meeting of the Coordination Committee between the Palestinian Government and the Board of Peace on the margin of the Palestine Donor Group meeting in Brussels. The Kingdom of Bahrain calls for removing all obstacles before the work of the Board of Peace as a transitional administrative entity with international legal personality that will set the framework to coordinate funding for the redevelopment of Gaza according to the comprehensive plan and in line with relevant principles of international law until the Palestinian Authority completes its reform program. The Kingdom of Bahrain highlights the importance of early recovery and reconstruction in Gaza. We emphasize the importance of deploying the international stabilization force in Gaza and the need for a full Israeli withdrawal. Second, the Kingdom of Bahrain expresses a steep concern regarding the tragic humanitarian situation facing two million Palestinians in Gaza. We reaffirm the importance of a full resumption of humanitarian assistance into Gaza in cooperation with the Board of Peace. We warn of the repercussions of denying Palestinian children their rights guaranteed by international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law. Therefore, The Kingdom of Bahrain, represented by the Royal Humanitarian Foundation, signed a cooperation agreement with the Jerusalem Development Fund to support the Bahraini endowment for education and orphans, and the Kingdom is thus the first country to implement an endowment project in Jerusalem. address the situation in Gaza without addressing the situation in the West Bank, which is witnessing troubling developments as a result of tensions and notably the alarming frequency of settlements and settler violence. The Kingdom of Bahrain calls for abiding by achieving joint understandings instead of imposing unilateral measures to put an end to all settlement activities in Palestinian territory and to meet all relevant legal obligations. The Kingdom would like to highlight the U.S.-GCC ministerial statement issued in the capital, Al Manama, on the 25th of June, which includes objection to the annexation of the West Bank, and which reaffirmed that no one will be forced to leave Gaza, and those who left are free to come back. The Kingdom of Bahrain renews its condemnation to all religious violations in Jerusalem. We also value the custodianship of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan of Christian and Islamic holy sites and the role of the Kingdom of Morocco in leading Al-Quds Committee. We also highlight the conference on the question of Jerusalem that was held in Cairo. in cooperation with the UN Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. Third and finally, the Kingdom of Bahrain calls for supporting the Palestinian Government, which is carrying out significant reform efforts. The Kingdom also welcomes all UN and international efforts and initiatives that call for integration, and we call for their full integration and coordination as they all aim to achieve the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, to strengthen their steadfastness on their territory, and to ensure their participation in reconstruction efforts. In conclusion, the Kingdom of Bahrain reaffirms that the building block for a safe, stable, prosperous and sustainable regional environment is the establishment of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state along the lines of June 4, 1967, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side with the state of Israel, pursuant to the principles of international law, the Arab Peace Initiative, relevant resolutions of international legitimacy, and Palestine should receive full membership at the United Nations. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the representative of Bahrain for their statement, and I give the floor to the representative of Colombia.

Thank you, Madam President. I'd like to thank Special Coordinator Al-Akbarow for his briefing, and I greet the delegations joining us at this meeting. Almost 10 months have passed now since the implementation of the peace plan began. Since then, Israel has killed more than 1,100 Palestinians and attacks on densely populated areas have continued to claim civilian lives and destroy the already threadbare infrastructure. It's difficult to characterize this reality as a ceasefire. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains catastrophic and the living conditions of the population have barely changed. The humanitarian response shouldn't be measured by the number of trucks entering Gaza. The question is rather, does the population have access to drinking water, sanitation, enough and nutritious food, medical care, education, and decent housing? However much an alternative reality is depicted to this Council, the response to this question is no. There are no decent living conditions in Gaza as a result of the lack of compliance incumbent on the occupying power under international law. While the Palestinian population continues to be confined to increasingly small and fragmented areas, high-ranking Israeli officials continue to promote a hateful rhetoric, encouraging the expansion of settlements, settler violence, forced displacement and ethnic cleansing in Gaza and the West Bank. Colombia has been clear regarding the principles that should guide the implementation of resolution 2803. They are respect for the right of the Palestinian people to self determination, to decide on their governance and their own future, the rejection of any demographic or territorial change, the central role of the United Nations in the humanitarian response and respect for the principle of humanity, neutrality and independence, and finally the immediate and unconditional beginning of Gaza's reconstruction. However, the facts reveal that the architecture of occupation is becoming more entrenched. Settlement expansion, settler violence, the financial suffocation of the Palestinian Authority and incitement to hatred are all part and parcel of a same policy to consolidate an illegal reality that is incompatible with the two state solution. No peace plan will be credible if it merely administers the consequences of the genocide without removing its root causes, beginning with the end of the illegal occupation. Madam President, the situation in Lebanon also remains worrisome. While we do welcome the continuing conversations and the agreements reached recently, which represent a first encouraging step towards de escalation, such progress falls short in light of the scale and severity of the situation. Colombia roundly condemns all action that violates the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon, the persistent erosion of the country's peace and security, doesn't only have devastating and immediate consequences for its population, but also compromises the country's long term development and stability. Alongside this, Israel is continuing in its war against the truth, the smear campaigns and campaigns making rash accusations against journalists, humanitarian workers, human rights defenders and UN officials. not only endanger their lives, but they also seek to silence those who are documenting the reality on the ground. This is a policy aimed at weakening international verification and accountability mechanisms, further eroding the principles that are essential for the protection of the civilian population. The impunity with which Israel has conducted this genocide calls into question the validity of the international order and the future of a system based on the sovereign equality of states, on justice and respect for international law, as opposed to an order in which the law of the strongest and the idea that some lives are worth more than others prevail. The United Nations was born to preserve succeeding generations from the scourge of war, to reaffirm the dignity and worth of the human person, and to create the right conditions for justice and international law to prevail over force. Today it falls to this Council to demonstrate that these principles remain valid because When law ceases to protect a people, it begins to lose its ability to protect us all. Thank you very much.
I thank the representative of Colombia for her statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of Latvia.

Thank you, Madam President. I thank Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Alaqbarah for his briefing. Madam President, At a time when the international community is making a united effort to resolve the conflict in the wider Middle East, Iran has reignited the crisis by targeting ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and conducting yet another campaign of reckless attacks against its neighbors, Bahrain, Iraq, Kuwait, and Qatar, as well as Jordan. Iran has also continued to undermine Yemen's sovereignty, including through recent unauthorized flights into Sana'a and Hodeidah. Iran must abandon any attempts to disrupt free and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. And in the same vein, Iran-supported Houthis must cease their threats and attacks against commercial shipping, imposing unlawful blockade in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait, and their attacks against Saudi Arabia. which threaten freedom of navigation, international trade, and regional stability, and risk drawing Yemen into a wider regional conflict. By launching an attack against Syria on 17th of July, Iran demonstrated that it prioritizes its own strategic objectives and the preservation of its disruptive influence in the region over Syria's post-war stabilization efforts. Iran's unjustified aggression blatantly disregards the memorandum of understanding threaten regional stability, and constitute a flagrant violation of the sovereignty, security, and territorial integrity of the respective countries. Latvia categorically condemns these attacks, and we express full solidarity with our Gulf partners, as well as Jordan, Iraq, and Syria. The wars in the Gulf and Ukraine are becoming increasingly interconnected, with Russia and Iran acting as mutually reinforcing drivers of instability across both regions. Russian-Iranian cooperation is no longer just a tactical partnership. It is a long-term strategic alliance based on shared interests to weaken the challenge of the international security and strengthen the military capabilities of both countries, leading to irregular migration flows. Russia has repeatedly relaxed visa rules, facilitated transit, provided logistical support, and used disinformation to channel migrants from the conflict areas of the Middle East and Africa toward EU borders, instrumentalizing the consequences of the conflicts it helped to spread. We reiterate our support for the resumption of meaningful negotiations between the United States and Iran. and appreciate the mediating efforts of Pakistan and Qatar, among others. In order for diplomacy to succeed, a complete cessation of hostilities and free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz is needed, in full compliance with the MOU and Resolution 2817. On Lebanon, we welcome the ongoing peace negotiations between Lebanon and Israel under the auspices of the United States. which pursue the same objectives as the resolution 1701, to secure a permanent ceasefire, achieve a sustainable solution to the conflict and provide lasting peace. We commend the conclusion of the 26 June trilateral framework agreement providing for the deployment of the Lebanese armed forces throughout the southern part of the country, disarmament of Hezbollah and withdrawal of Israel forces from Lebanon. Launching the pilot zones Plan represents a tangible step towards the implementation of this framework. We call for the continuation of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel to reach a comprehensive and sustainable agreement, restoring Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity while addressing Israel's security concerns. This effort also requires an end to Iran's support for and influence over Hezbollah. which undermines Lebanon's sovereignty and the prospects for lasting peace. The international community must continue and reinforce its support to Lebanon's government and armed forces to take full control of the territory and the monopoly of weapons. Adjusted, credible, and impartial UN presence in Lebanon will be essential to oversee the implementation of the resolution 1701 after the drawdown of UNIFIL. as well as the comprehensive bilateral agreement once it is reached. Madam President, in Gaza, further progress on implementing Resolution 2803 and the comprehensive peace plan put forward by President Trump is urgently needed. In this regard, all parties must abide by their commitments. Hamas and non-state armed groups must accept the plan proposed by the Board of Peace, disarm, and relinquish their power. The ongoing daily strikes in Gaza and the resulting Palestinian civilian casualties must stop. The deployment of the ISF and the Palestinian police, as well as withdrawal of the IDF, must provide a pathway for stabilization. The long-delayed recovery of the entire Gaza Strip through the work of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza must be enabled urgently. We welcome the recent meeting of the Palestine donor group and launching the Team Gaza initiative to support reconstruction and healthcare. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains extremely challenging. Insecurity, access restrictions, and repeated displacements continue to constrain humanitarian operations. Limited and unpredictable flows of humanitarian goods are increasing hunger, restricting the availability of essential supplies, and placing additional pressure on a nearly collapsed health system. Sustained, safe, and predictable humanitarian access remains critical to enable an effective response. And in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, the human rights, humanitarian, and security situation keeps deteriorating. Expansion of Israeli settlements, including in the E1 area, is ongoing, with increasing numbers of Palestinian families being evicted from their homes. Settler violence continues, and we call on Israel to ensure accountability for all committed assaults and killings and fully respect all of its legal obligations. A political solution encompassing Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is the only way to sustainable peace based on the two-state solution as defined by the Security Council resolutions and the New York Declaration. Addressing the security concerns and legitimate aspirations of both Israelis and Palestinians requires renewed momentum in the implementation of the comprehensive plan and genuine engagement by all parties. On Syria, Syria's achievements by pursuing the path of stability and recovery stand out against the backdrop of broader regional turmoil and inspire hope that positive change is possible. And we welcome the Secretary General's recent visit to Syria and trust that UN's continued support will reinforce Syria's political transition, reconstruction and transitional justice. In conclusion, Madam President, Latvia remains committed to achieving comprehensive and lasting peace in the Middle East, as well as fully restoring freedom of navigation, and expresses its readiness to continue efforts alongside regional and global partners to achieve the shared goal.

Thank you.
I thank the representative of Latvia for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of Pakistan.

Thank you, Madam President. This debate is an important opportunity for a holistic assessment of the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question. The Deputy Special Coordinator's briefing and the detailed statements in the chamber testify that the occupied Palestinian territory remains in dire straits. While the ceasefire and President Trump's comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict have provided an important opportunity to alleviate humanitarian suffering, and advance a credible pathway to Palestinian self-determination and statehood, delays in full implementation of these efforts require our urgent attention. It is imperative to uphold the commitments reflected in the peace plan and Resolution 2803 that endorsed it. Failure to act now risks irreparably undermining the prospects for a just and lasting peace. Developments in the West Bank are a matter of grave concern. Continued settlement expansion, the establishment of new settlement outposts, and increased incidents of settler violence are altering the demographic and geographic character of the occupied Palestinian territory. In this context, the so-called Crimson Thread project, a planned 500 kilometer network of walls and military roads bisecting the Jordan Valley, also raises serious concerns, as these efforts to isolate Palestinian communities and sever the Jordan Valley from the rest of the West Bank will undermine the viability and territorial contiguity of a future Palestinian state. The foreign ministers of the Group of Eight Arab and Islamic countries, including Pakistan, have also condemned in the strongest terms the Israeli escalation at Al-Aqsa Mosque, Al-Haram Al-Sharif, particularly the continued mass incursions by settlers. They stress that these provocative actions constitute a flagrant violation of international law, the relevant UN resolutions, and the historical and legal status quo at the holy sites in the occupied East Jerusalem. Madam President, in Gaza, the humanitarian situation is extremely fragile. The ceasefire, and the implementation of elements of the peace plan have yielded some improvements. However, 59% of the population still faces crisis-level food insecurity. And notably, since the ceasefire, over 1,100 Palestinians have been killed. And that calls into question the full and faithful implementation of the plan. Nearly two million people remain confined to just 30% of Gaza's territory. and enduring catastrophic living conditions. There are also reports of a massive earthen barrier being constructed across Gaza, entrenching Israeli occupation and control over nearly 70% of the territory. Against this backdrop, the Security Council should act with unity and support the full implementation of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and Security Council Resolution 2803, demand an immediate halt to all settlement activities and reject any attempts at annexation, forced displacement or alteration of the demographic and geographic character of the occupied Palestinian territory in accordance with relevant UNSC resolutions, including 2334, ensure international protection for the Palestinian people, as also urged by President Abbas in his recent letter to the Council, and hold accountable those responsible for crimes and violations committed against civilians, and secure the immediate unconditional release of withheld Palestinian revenues to enable the Palestinian Authority to continue delivering essential public services. Madam President, the only credible path to a just and lasting peace is the establishment of an independent, sovereign, contiguous, and viable state of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. In the broader context, Pakistan continues to follow with deep concern the recent developments that are further escalating regional tensions. Pakistan reiterates its strong support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all brotherly countries in the region and urges all sides to exercise restraint, take immediate steps towards de-escalation, and uphold respective commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. On its part, Pakistan remains committed to providing all support towards achieving lasting peace and stability in the region through dialogue and diplomacy. In Lebanon, the full implementation of resolution 1701 remains essential for achieving lasting peace and stability. Pakistan appreciates the diplomatic efforts led by the US to consolidate the cessation of hostilities and advance a durable peace in Lebanon. Pakistan also calls for full respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and reaffirms its support for the government's efforts in this new phase. The 1974 disengagement agreement and resolutions 338 and 497 must be fully respected. Israel must vacate its illegal occupation of all Arab territories. Pakistan supports a Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process for comprehensive and lasting peace in Yemen. Pakistan condemns attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and all attacks against commercial shipping, which threaten global trade and regional security. Pakistan is deeply concerned over attempts to drag the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia into the conflict in the Middle East and reiterates its unwavering support for the security, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and prosperity of the brotherly kingdom. Madam President, lasting peace in the Middle East will remain elusive as long as occupation persists and the legitimate aspirations of the Palestinian people for self-determination remain unfulfilled. Pakistan continues to stand in unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people and will support all genuine efforts aimed at achieving a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace based on relevant UN Security Council resolutions and international legitimacy. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Pakistan for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of China.

Madam President, I thank Deputy Special Coordinator Alaa Baraf for his briefing. The situation in the Middle East continues to escalate with hotspot issues affecting one another, casting a shadow of conflict over the entire region. Restoring peace is the fervent hope of the people there, and achieving a ceasefire to end violence must be their overriding priority. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East conflict and must not be ignored or marginalized. Only by achieving a comprehensive, just, and lasting solution to the Palestinian issue can we break the vicious cycle of recurring conflicts in the Middle East and truly usher in the dawn of peace. I would like to emphasize three points. First, civilian suffering cannot continue, and peace and stability in Gaza must be restored. The Gaza ceasefire agreement was reached more than nine months ago, yet bombings and blockade continue, and more than two million people remain trapped in the threat of death and displacement. Lasting security can only be built on respect and mutual trust. Fighting and ruins breed only hatred and division or confrontation. Gaza is not a perpetual battlefield, and suffering and turmoil are certainly not the destiny for Gazans. We call on Israel and All parties concerned to fully implement the ceasefire agreement and achieve a genuine lasting ceasefire in Gaza. Israel must fulfill its obligations under international humanitarian law, cease restricting humanitarian supplies into Gaza, and ensure that humanitarian agencies, including UNRWA, can carry out their aid operations. Second, the international rule of law must not be compromised, and tensions in the West Bank must be eased. The current settler violence in the West Bank is appalling, resulting in large civilian casualties and destruction of homes. The occupying power is speeding up its settlement expansion and eroding Palestinian territory. Despite strong appeals from the international community, the situation in the West Bank continues to worsen. A key reason for this is the unrealized investigation and accountability and the persistence of impunity. International law and Council Resolution 2334 must be respected and abided by, and any double standards and selective applications are unacceptable. We urge Israel to immediately cease settlement activities, take concrete actions to curb violence, and ensure strict accountability for all attacks. The West Bank economy is already struggling. Israel should return the tax revenue as soon as possible and lift unreasonable restrictions on the West Bank. Third, fairness and justice must not be absent. We must push for implementing the two-state solution. For decades, the Palestine-Israel situation has seen repeated turbulence. The problem lies in the two-state solution being realized only halfway. Israel became an independent state a long time ago, but a Palestinian state remains a distant prospect. The international community must take firmly anchor to the general direction of the two-state solution, put greater efforts, and take irreversible action. Any arrangement or establishment of new mechanisms must adhere to the principle of Palestinians governing Palestine, respect the will of the Palestinian people, and promote rather than undermine the two-state solution. Any dangerous attempt to change the territorial and demographic composition of Palestine will severely undermine the foundation for the two-state solution and must be firmly opposed. China supports the early establishment of an independent Palestinian state with full sovereignty based on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. President, China is deeply concerned with the recent escalation of tension in the Gulf region of the Middle East. The MOU signed over a month ago is a valuable achievement of the many through good offices and mediation. It embodies the hope of the people in the Middle East to end the war for peace and stability, and these efforts should not go to waste. Now the door has opened for negotiation. It should not be shut. As long as there is still hope for peace, our efforts should not be abandoned. The most urgent task now is to adhere to the path of diffusing disputes through negotiations and return to implementing the MOU consensus. China will continue to support the good offices of Pakistan and others, early resumption of dialogue and negotiations by parties concerned, early resumption of the normal and safe passage of the Strait of Hormuz, improvement of relations among neighboring countries, and joint pursuit of collective security for the Gulf states. The Red Sea is an important route for international trade. All parties concerned should respect respect the rights of navigation in the Red Sea for by commercial vessels of all countries in accordance with international law, respect the sovereignty, security and territorial integrity of all nations and jointly safeguard the safety and unimpeded flow of international shipping lanes. All parties concerned should continue to properly diffuse conflicts and differences through dialogue and consultation and avoid taking actions that exacerbate confrontation. We welcome the de-escalation in the Lebanon-Israel situation. All parties concerned should cease hostilities and fully implement Resolution 1701 and Israel should withdraw all its troops from Lebanon. China supports Syria in maintaining sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity. Golan Heights is an occupied Syrian territory recognized by the international community, and the 1974 disengagement agreement should be abided by. The Middle East belongs to the people of the Middle East. It should not become an arena for great power rivalry or a victim of geopolitics. China will continue to uphold the spirit of the four-point proposal put forward by President Xi Jinping on maintaining and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East. We will work together with the international community to advance political solutions to regional hotspot issues, support regional countries in upholding their autonomy and rebuilding mutual trust, build a new regional security architecture adapted to evolving circumstances, and achieve lasting peace and stability in the Middle East. Thank you, Madam President.

I thank the representative of China for the statement. I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Distinguished members of the Council, ladies and gentlemen, the Democratic Republic of the Congo would like to thank Mr. Ramiz Alagbarov, Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process within the Office for the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator. We thank him for his briefing, which enlightened the Council relating to the recent developments in the region. My delegation remains alarmed by the persistent humanitarian and security crisis in the Gaza Strip, as well as by the continued worsening of the situation in the West Bank, including in East Jerusalem. Despite the progress made thanks to the ceasefire established pursuant to resolution 2803 of 2025, the civilian population continues to endure considerable suffering and the prospects for lasting peace remain fragile. The DRC welcomes the progress made in implementing the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict, particularly the maintenance of the ceasefire, the release of all of the hostages, as well as the increase in humanitarian aid. This progress speaks to the fact that dialogue and diplomacy can lead to tangible outcomes when they enjoy sincere commitment from all parties. Nonetheless, these gains remain fragile. We note with concern that several essential parts of the plan are pending. The negotiations relating to the roadmap have still not been finalised, the deployment of the international stabilisation force has yet to begin, Gaza's transitional administration has not yet been able to fully assume its responsibilities, and the other necessary conditions have not yet been met. The Democratic Republic of the Congo encourages all parties to demonstrate restraint and to pursue good faith negotiations so as to ensure an implementation of the provisions of resolution 2803. Distinguished members of the Council, the humanitarian situation continues to demand the urgent attention of the international community. While aid flows have significantly increased, The needs remain immense. Millions of people are still displaced. Access to healthcare, to drinking water, electricity, education and basic services remains limited, while much of the civilian infrastructure has been destroyed. The Democratic Republic of the Congo reaffirms that humanitarian assistance must be provided in a continued, safe, rapid and unhindered manner in accordance with international humanitarian law. We call on all parties to facilitate the work of United Nations agencies and of humanitarian organisations so that they can effectively respond to the needs of the civilian population. My delegation also continues to follow closely the development of the situation in the West Bank, which risks further jeopardising the prospects for a fair, lasting and negotiated peace. The Democratic Republic of the Congo reaffirms its commitment to respect for international law, the United Nations Charter and the relevant resolutions of the Security Council. We call on all parties to refrain from any action likely to fuel tensions or to compromise ongoing diplomatic efforts. My delegation takes note of the efforts undertaken by the Board of Peace, by guarantor states and international partners to facilitate the transition and the re-establishment of civilian institutions in Gaza. We hope that the transitional mechanisms, including the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, the International Stabilisation Force, will be able to be deployed amidst a climate of trust, with the agreement of the parties concerned and with full respect for international law. We also encourage the States and international partners that have pledged financial contributions to speed up the disbursement of the pledged funds so as to support economic recovery and the restoration of the essential services for the benefit of the civilian population. The Democratic Republic of the Congo remains convinced that no lasting solution will result from the use of force, only a political dynamic based on dialogue, mutual respect, Trust and good faith will lay the foundations for a lasting peace and long term stability in the Middle East. To conclude, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaffirms its readiness to pursue, alongside other members of the Security Council, all efforts to foster a lasting de escalation. We call on all parties to demonstrate restraint, to preserve the ceasefire, and to ensure the protection of the civilian population, to guarantee safe, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access, and to focus on the path of dialogue and diplomacy so as to establish the conditions for a fair, comprehensive, and lasting peace in the Middle East. Thank you. I resume my function as President of the Council. I wish to remind all speakers to limit their statements to no more than three minutes in order to enable the Council to carry out its work expeditiously. The flashing light on the microphone will prompt speakers to bring their remarks to a close after three minutes. I now give the floor to His Excellency Mr. Kholi Sek, Chair of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People.

Thank you very much, Madam President. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, I would like to thank the Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Ramiz Alghbarah, for his briefing. The Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestine People addresses the Council with deep concern. Over the last three months, The situation in the occupied Palestinian territory has not seen any noticeable improvements. The current escalation is the continuation of a systematic policy of terror that, as the committee has underscored for decades, seeks to dismantle the Palestinian presence and deny the Palestinian people their inalienable rights. In Gaza, the ceasefire remains fragile and incomplete. It has not put an end to the suffering of civilians. Since the ceasefire was announced, more than 1,000 Palestinians have reportedly been killed and thousands more injured. The majority of the population remains displaced, confined to shrinking areas, and exposed to hunger, disease, and insecurity. UNRWA and other United Nations agencies must be able to fully carry out their activities. And the Security Council must ensure full implementation of Resolution 2803, guarantee unhindered humanitarian access, ensure the protection of civilians, and support the start of reconstruction efforts, while reaffirming that Gaza remains an integral part of the occupied Palestinian territory. The most recent report of the Secretary General on conflict related sexual violence also documents patterns of sexual violence against Palestinian detainees. This means that there is a need for immediate protection for victims and survivors, urgent independent investigations, and full accountability for those responsible at every level. The same goes for the demolitions, evictions, settler violence, military operations, and restrictions on movement. These actions are carried out in full impunity and in violation of international law, and they are designed to terrorize the Palestinian population. Madam President, Jerusalem remains at the heart of the question of Palestine. On July 18th, the committee, together with the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, convened the 2026 conference on the question of Jerusalem in Cairo. The participants stressed the need to preserve the historic and legal status quo of the holy sites to protect freedom of worship and to defend the Palestinian presence, rights, and sovereignty in occupied East Jerusalem. Madam President, the path forward is clear. International law must be respected. The two-state solution must be preserved through concrete actions, including by pursuing efforts that have been undertaken in the context of the conference on the two-state solution in 2025. The unlawful occupation must end. The Palestinian people must exercise their inalienable rights, including their rights to self-determination, independence, and return. I thank you.
I thank His Excellency Mr. Saif for his statement. And I now give the floor to the representative of Kazakhstan.

Thank you, Madam President. I thank you for convening today's open debate and express appreciation to Mr. Amizahov for his valuable briefing. Madam President, Kazakhstan remains deeply concerned by the deterioration of the situation in the Middle East and by the wider impact of regional tensions on international peace and security. The Palestinian question remains at the heart of the crisis in the Middle East. Kazakhstan reaffirms its support for a just, comprehensive, and lasting settlement based on the two-state solution. We underscore the indispensable role of the United Nations, including UNRWA and Security Council Resolution 2803, in supporting the Palestinian people and advancing recovery and reconstruction. Humanitarian relief should be devoted to early recovery and reconstruction under the United Nations coordination. These efforts should reflect Palestinian priorities and contribute to the reunification of Gaza and the West Bank within the framework of a viable Palestinian state. Moreover, we invite to utilize the potential of the Islamic Organization for Food Security headquartered in Astana, which has already delivered aid to Afghanistan, Syria, and Gaza. Madam President, recent developments in the Gulf region once again show how quickly tensions can escalate, with consequences extending far beyond the immediate area of conflict. This dangerous crisis threatens to drive the Middle East deeper into uncharted waters, placing regional security and global supply chains under severe strain. Developments affecting the Strait of Hormuz are a reminder that regional instability can affect international trade, transport, and energy supplies, as well as states not party to the conflict. Kazakhstan is therefore concerned by attacks on civilian vessels and critical civilian infrastructure. Such attacks undermine confidence in transport routes, disrupt lawful economic activities, and increase risks to global energy security. They must stop, and practical steps are needed to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and the protection of civilian infrastructure in line with international law. In this context, we note the important role played by countries of the Gulf region in maintaining regional stability, supporting dialogue, and ensuring the resilience of global energy and trade systems. Their constructive engagement remains essential for de-escalation and confidence building. Recent developments in the region once again warn us from dangerous escalation. Non-parties of the conflict should not be drawn in it. Kazakhstan remains committed to working with all partners in support of peace, security, and stability in the Middle East and beyond. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Kazakhstan for the statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of the Republic of Korea.

Thank you, Madam President. I thank Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Al-Nakhaburov for his valuable briefing. Nine months have passed since the endorsement of the Gaza Comprehensive Peace Plan by the Security Council Resolution 2803. which established a framework to end the conflict in Gaza and chart a path toward a sustainable peace. We welcome the board of peace efforts and ongoing steps to establish transitional governance in Gaza. The recent declaration by Hamas of its intention to transfer authority to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is an increasing sign for the future progress. However, while some progress has been made since the announcement of the cease fire, the Republic of Korea is deeply concerned that the progress toward the second phase has been largely stalled and the already dire humanitarian crisis on the ground continue to worsen. To break the deadlock and prevent further regional destabilization, my delegation would like to emphasize three critical priorities. First, the implementation of Resolution 2803 must proceed in a balanced and accountable manner. The deadlock cannot be resolved unilaterally. Progress on the pace withdrawal of the IDF and deployment of the ISF and Hamas decommissioning of weapons all remain closely linked. These interdependent elements require renewed political commitment and mutual trust and sustained engagement by all key stakeholders. Second, Gaza requires unhindered humanitarian access at scale immediately. It is very alarming that nearly 1,200 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire, and that 90% of Gaza's population still remains forcibly displaced and concentrated into less than a third of the strip. Families are enduring immense hardship and severe shortage of all basic necessities, including food, while humanitarian operations face best constraint. Measures to revoke licenses for key international NGOs severely compound an already fragile relief environment. My government underscores that humanitarian aid must reach civilians rapidly and safely and without obstruction, and all parties must respect international humanitarian law under all circumstances. Third, we must prevent the further fragmentation of the occupied Palestinian territory. We remain seriously troubled by the development in the occupied West Bank, including illegal settlement expansion and nearly daily settler violence, as well as deteriorating economic conditions.
